articles.title: The Relational Capacity Framework: A Lens for AI-Mediated Relationality
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A growing literature examines the impact of engaging with AI chatbots on our relationality: our ability to form relationships with others, maintain them through life's changes, and exit when needed. Currently, substantial work focuses on purpose-built AI companions (e.g. Replika, Character.AI), with less work investigating socioemotional uses of the more widely-used general-purpose chatbots. articles.title: The Drawing You Watch Is the Portrait You Keep: A Replayable Machine Portrait Studio
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ask an image model for your portrait and a finished picture arrives: no first line, no second thoughts, no record of how it got there, and a different picture if you ask again. I built a portrait studio that works the other way. A sitter chooses one of eight fictional artists, each written with a city, a medium and a tempo of its own, holds still for 8 to 12 seconds, and watches a drawing of themselves appear over 44 seconds. articles.title: A Taxonomy-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Retrieval Effectiveness and Fairness Evaluation in Hiring
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While machine learning hiring tools are ubiquitous, the need for privacy regulations and commercial sensitivity makes public benchmarking legally complex. We address this challenge by introducing a taxonomy-driven, fully synthetic HR dataset and benchmark to simultaneously evaluate retrieval effectiveness and algorithmic fairness. Grounded in 660K real freelancer profiles, our multilingual corpus features candidate profiles, project briefs, and counterfactual demographic twins. articles.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. articles.title: Entering a New Domain in the Era of Generative AI: An Autoethnography of Solo Game Development as a Bioinformatics Educator
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid improvement of generative AI (GenAI) not only increased the efficiency of practice but also empowered individuals with capabilities to explore new domains. However, identity formation in the wake of such empowerment remains understudied. We use an autoethnography to understand identity formation in the context of solo game development as a bioinformatics educator. articles.title: Strategic Competition and Convergence in LLM Leaderboards
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Leaderboards are a popular way to compare large language model (LLM) capabilities and can influence how model developers invest resources. We ask when competition on leaderboards leads developers to produce models with similar capability profiles, which we call monoculture, or similar performance levels. We study this by formulating leaderboard competition as a game in which model developers invest resources across capabilities to maximize their win rate. articles.title: Subjective Experience in AI Systems: What Do AI Researchers and the Public Believe?
articles.summary: arXiv:2506.11945v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whether AI systems are perceived to have subjective experience has scientific, ethical, and governance implications. Yet little is known about how AI researchers and the public view this possibility. We surveyed 582 AI researchers who published in leading AI venues and 825 nationally representative US adults about the likelihood, identification, and governance of AI systems with subjective experience. articles.title: Budgeting Discretion: Theory and Evidence on Street-Level Decision-Making
articles.summary: arXiv:2602.10039v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Street-level bureaucrats, such as caseworkers, triage nurses, and school administrators, operate under a fundamental tension. Official policy on who to prioritize may conflict with bureaucrats' estimation of who would benefit most. The theory of street-level bureaucracy argues that frontline agents bridge this gap, overriding policy when professional judgment identifies opportunities to improve outcomes. articles.title: Decomposing Yes-No Bias in LLM Moral Judgment: Stance, Position, Word, and Verdict
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.05552v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly issue binary verdicts - safety gates, judge decisions, value probes - and the answer is read as the model's judgment. A settled judgment should be coherent across paired phrasings of the same question: yes to "do you approve?" should mirror no to "do you oppose?". articles.title: Making Sense of Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.38026v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recommendation-driven platforms can reshape not only what users see, but also who becomes visible and how community boundaries are negotiated.
